title: fix(release): resolve a run-list count above a short page by walking the unfiltered runs
body:
Fixes #33195

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么：稳定发布「在途」读取器（快照通道 stable-lane 与发布在途回填守卫共用）遇到 GitHub 状态过滤「总数比这一页列出的多、页又没满」并且重读三次仍不一致时，不再直接判 NOT MEASURED，而是往回翻 31 天内的不过滤运行列表、逐个按 id 读状态：找到被过滤漏掉的真实在途运行就照常判在途并拒绝；找不到就把「计数指向的运行不存在」连同翻过的范围写进读数行后放行。
- 为什么改：11-11 与 11-14 两次每日快照都因「计数 2、只列出本运行」被拒并报假卡；实测两次 release.yml 都只有本运行活着，而上一次加的重读修复（#32467）在 11-14 三次重读都没消掉这个多出来的 1。
- 风险与回滚：仍是 fail-closed：翻页任一页读不到、行没有创建时间、60 页内既没到 31 天边界也没到历史起点、或本运行重试预算已用尽，都照旧拒绝；只动两个脚本，不动 workflow 与 `version` 脚本链；回滚即还原本 PR。
- 先看：`scripts/release-pending-publish.mjs` 的 `readWholeRunList` / `resolveShortPage` / `walkRunList`（放行条件就在 `resolveShortPage` 的 proof 分支）；`scripts/ci/snapshot-next.mjs` 的 `readStableLane` 合并段；`collectWaitingRuns` 的 `jobs: null`。
- 两分钟验证：`node scripts/release-pending-publish.mjs --self-test && node scripts/ci/snapshot-next.mjs --self-test`，预期 161 例 / 36 组、197 例 / 23 组全过。
- 需要你做的：无，席位落地。

## What changes

The ruling is A on #33195 (Ruling-ref 6879496577, recorded in 6879884762).

- `scripts/release-pending-publish.mjs`, `readWholeRunList`: the re-read ladder is unchanged. When it ends with a status filter's `total_count` still above a page that is NOT full, the new `resolveShortPage` takes over. It walks the workflow's unfiltered run list newest first (`page=N`, 100 each) with `walkRunList`, back at most `RUN_WALK_DAYS` (31) or to the start of history. Every walked run whose row carries the filtered status and is not on the page is read by id. A direct read in that status is a row that lagged the filter, and it is added to the runs judged. The readings line then records one of three proofs:
  - `count N over page M names no run: the walk of K runs back to DATE (BOUND, P pages) found none other`
  - `... found L more in STATUS [ids], whose row(s) lagged the filter`
  - the same, plus `the other X name(s) no run`
- Still throws, as before: a count above a FULL page; a count that is no number; a spent retry budget before the ladder ends. Newly throws: an unread walk page (5xx after the retries, or any non-200); a walk row with no `created_at`; a walk that reaches neither bound within `RUN_WALK_MAX_PAGES` (60); a candidate the direct read cannot answer. Each is the reader's own NOT MEASURED, which `publishInFlight` maps to `unreadable` and `stable-lane` to NOT MEASURED.
- `collectPublishRuns` / `publishInFlight` take an optional `now` (default `Date.now()`) that dates the walk's bound.
- `collectWaitingRuns`: a run it does not read past its status now carries `jobs: null` (NOT READ), never `[]`. `judgeWaitingRuns` reads `jobs` only for `waiting` runs, which are always read, so the sweep is unchanged; the new pin covers it.
- `scripts/ci/snapshot-next.mjs`, `readStableLane`: it passes `now` to both readers. The merge reads `null` as NOT READ: the first reading that read the jobs speaks for the run, empty list included. A run still in flight whose jobs neither reader read has them read here. That is an older version commit's push run, which only the waiting reader probes. A publish running in such a run now refuses instead of merging as a run holding no job; the readings line names the runs read this way. `stableLane` takes an optional `now` for the self-test.

## Tests

Both self-tests drive the real readers over stubbed Actions APIs.

- `release-pending-publish --self-test`: 153 → 161 cases, 36 batteries. The in-flight listing battery is renamed to what it now pins, and its floor goes 7 → 14. Its case "a count still above the page on every read the ladder allows -> unreadable" becomes:
  - the 11-14 reading: count 2 over the calling run alone, a walk listing no other run in progress → clear, with the proof line; no completed row read; the queued filter read after it;
  - a dispatch run the rows left out but the walk lists → read by id, jobs read, publish in flight;
  - a walk row in progress whose direct read says completed → not added;
  - a walk explaining part of the excess → that run judged, the rest recorded as naming no run;
  - an unread walk page → unreadable, for the publish and the image alike;
  - a walk reaching neither bound in 60 pages → unreadable;
  - a walk stopping at the 31-day bound → the proof names the bound;
  - a walk row with no `created_at` → unreadable.

  The earlier "count over an empty page → unreadable" case now pins the unread-walk branch. The waiting-runs battery gains: "a version-commit push run in flight → jobs null, not read; the sweep leaves it untouched".
- `snapshot-next --self-test`: 194 → 197 cases, 23 batteries. The stable-lane battery floor goes 13 → 16. The pinned "a count still above the page after every re-read the run allows THROWS" becomes three cases:
  - ⭐ the 11-14 reading passes, with the proof on the readings line;
  - ⛔ a walk finding a run in progress the rows left out → its jobs are read, and its stable publish refuses;
  - ⛔ an unread walk page still THROWS (NOT MEASURED).

  Plus ⛔ an older version commit's push run in flight, found by the waiting reader alone → its jobs are read in `readStableLane`, and its publish refuses.

No ablation: `.claude/agents/os-dev.md` (标准条款) exempts scripts from ablation.

## Acceptance notes

**Measured vs documented-only (the 31-day bound and the walk):**

- Documented by GitHub, NOT measured here: a job held at an environment fails after 30 days, and a run can be re-run only within 30 days of its first attempt. Those two windows are the only ways a run created earlier than the bound can newly ENTER `in_progress` or `queued`. `RUN_WALK_DAYS = 31` is that plus one day of margin.
- Measured, 2026-11-14:
  - A run stuck in a status since before the bound is already a row on the filter's page: ci.yml's `in_progress` filter lists run 31118082788, created 2026-08-06 (attempt 2), still `in_progress`.
  - At both refusals (runs 42938356503 on 11-11 and 43540146973 on 11-14), no release.yml run other than the lane's own was alive. That comes from a sweep of all 3,564 release.yml runs created 10-12..11-14 (paged by `page=N`; no other run's last update falls after the lane run started). So the walk would have explained both as phantom counts.
  - 135 samples of the `in_progress` filter on ci.yml, lint.yml and fleet-write.yml: 18 counts one above the page. In 4 the filter's rows lagged (the unfiltered list showed the run), so the count was the true witness. In 14 the count named no run either list showed.
  - In 75 id-level samples, the unfiltered newest page never omitted a live run the filter listed. The one difference was a run the filter still listed 2 s after it completed.
  - The unfiltered listing pages without the 1,000-result cap: page 36 answers rows from 2026-10-11, `total_count` 15062.
  - release.yml created about 108 runs a day over those 33 days, so a 31-day walk is about 34 pages. It is read only on a day the ladder ends short (2 of 8 lane days so far). The 60-page cap leaves the rate room to nearly double.
- Not measured: whether GitHub ever deletes a run mid-walk (offset paging would skip one row), and whether the unfiltered rows can lag a run newly entering `in_progress` (no sample showed it).

**Fence:** the `annotate-shipped` path, `.github/workflows/**` and the root `package.json` `version` script are untouched. `git diff --stat` covers the two files only.

**No changeset:** the root package is private, and `scripts/` ships in no package's `files[]` (precedent #32467, same two files, `skip-changeset`).
